requirements.requirement: Serve the supplied staged help content on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: nginx listened on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8080 and returned the staged root and nested help documents with content matching the supplied source. The same listener and matching nested content were observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Return permanent redirects from old /manual/ URLs to corresponding /help/ URLs while retaining the remaining path and query string.
requirements.summary: Root and nested manual URLs returned HTTP 301 with the expected help path and preserved query parameters. A nested redirect behaved identically after the node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Continue serving the supplied /status.txt document directly, without redirecting it.
requirements.summary: The endpoint returned HTTP 200 and its body matched the supplied status document by content and SHA-256 before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged after execution and reboot. nginx 1.26.3 was installed from the RHEL 10 AppStream repository, and package consistency remained healthy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart service and data state, an acknowledged reboot request and connection interruption, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, content, redirect, firewall, SELinux, platform, and package state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing nginx and resolver-selected dependencies, configuring nginx, applying persistent SELinux labels and port policy, opening port 8080, and enabling the service all directly supported the requested outcome. The retained root-only nginx rollback copy had a clear recovery role. The transient reboot unit implemented the mandatory restart protocol, and the temporary status verification file was removed within the same command. No failed services, damaged package state, unexplained listener, or abandoned verification file remained after execution.
